Designed purely for tip-time, the Cutwater is our take on the classic noserider for those under-chest-high log sessions. Our rocker is inspired by old-school shapers that flipped foam blanks around, nose-to-tail, to get maximum tail-kick and a low nose. A deep, natural, concave under its beak runs to a flat-bottom midsection and a super-swept square-tail. Dimensions like those, along with 50/50 rails, are why this board allows you to get a walk in while you ride. So, either lock yourself in the pocket or drag along for a slow dance on the tip.

Its weighted construction fearless before monster waves, this big gun runs chatter-free ahead of bone-crushing curls.

Looking for something for her home break, we worked up a slender funshape up to fit her advanced skills. Besides the graceful single-to-double concaves and tight little squash tail. we designed it as a low-rocker board with a flat entry and hotted it up with a curvy, spooned-out step deck forward. This board has the full outline fun-shape surfers want, but with performance elements pros look for.

models.name: The Bluntfish
models.description: This paipo is a collaboration between Jon Wegener and Grain surfboards and is hand-built and shaped in York Maine with a core of 100% recycled plastic bottles, combined with wood stringers. The bottom of the board is made from cedar and/or paulownia planks while the rails and deck is all natural cork from the Cork Oak Tree. These boards are the perfect blend of simplicity, functionality and sustainability and we believe represent one of the most fun ways to get out and enjoy some waves. A Jon Wegener original, the Bluntfish’s long rail line and wide tail make this a great candidate for small or mushy waves. This board provides an early entry and maximum trim on almost any wave. The blunt nose is great to hang onto while cranking turns. Available in: 42” & 48” *Note- Second two photos below show all models in this new construction.

Jon Wegener has long made the Pumpkin Seed, which is a close cousin to the Pepita. It’s best served with a steeper hollow wave where the outline allows for late drops with precision pivot turns into the pocket. models.name: The Puffin
models.description: Paipos hold a special place in our hearts, and if you've kicked around the shop over the years, you've seen lots of shapes and sizes in hollow and solid construction, using a wide range of materials including wood, cork, recycled PET, and more. The Puffin is our second hollow paipo ( the Leaf was the first) and is inspired by some early spoon kneeboards by the likes of George Greenough. Often the most challenging boards to build are the shortest ones, and the Puffin is no exception. The bottom has belly in the nose and a nice subtle concave coming off the tail. But that's not all. The deck is built in two pieces in order to accommodate the dished out spoon and tapering rails. This board is thin and wide through the tail, providing lots of planing surface, with a sweet concave deck to hold you in the pocket. Set up as a twin fin with FCS plugs, you have options for no fins, small single tab fins or larger keels, depending on your preference. If you like to surf prone (or even on your knees), this board is a must-have! Note, hollow paipos (unlike solid wood boards that are simply oiled) are glassed to seal them. So they require the same care of any glassed surfboard to prevent the glass from cracking. Specs: 4'2" x 20.5"

models.name: The Leaf
models.description: Finished Board Specs: 4'5" x 21.25" x 2 3/4" / Volume 31.89 L For 'Tailored Dims', we'll reach out with a form to tell us what you're thinking about. The Leaf is one of our earliest board models dating back to 2006. Based on a 1969 Paipo, this sweet little hollow board has a classic outline, very little rocker, and a miraculous number of reversing contours and curves that seem impossible in such a short board. Though it's designed to have an 8″ hi-aspect ratio single fin, we've started putting side-bite boxes in for micro twinzers. The narrow tail has increased thickness to add buoyancy and paddling power. Designed for large powerful waves, most people would ride this board prone, but skilled surfers have been known to surf it standing up. Put on your fins, and put all those boogie boarders to shame.

models.name: The Wherry
models.description: Finished Board Specs 5'8" x 20.5" x 2 9/16" / Volume- 31.4L 6’-0” x 21 1/16″ x 2 9/16″ / Volume- 34.2L 6’-4” x 21 11/16″ x 2 3/4″ / Volume- 39.9 L For 'Tailored Dims', we'll reach out with a form to tell us what you're thinking about. The Wherry is our modern fish, designed to excel in steeper wave conditions and push harder into the performance surfing realm. Named for the boats that bridge the gap between narrow racing shells wider rowboats, this sleek swallowtail is still a fish at heart, but with more finely tuned features taken from modern shortboards. Born from storm surf of New England, the Wherry likes a bit of power to the wave and is ready to shred! The Wherry features a more aggressive, pulled-in outline, narrowing the nose and tail from a traditional fish shape. Increased nose and tail rocker allow for steeper drops, tighter turns, and better fit into hollow sections. Full volume in the center allows easier paddling and earlier entry into waves, while the finely-tuned, down rails provide crucial grip on steeper faces and more extreme carving turns. Single concave under the front foot for lift and speed transitioning to a spiral “V” out the tail, further increasing the rail to rail maneuverability of this fish. Available as a twin or quad fin. Action shots by Chris Gauthier, Elli Thor, Brayden Rudert, Joseph Allison, and Amanda Prifti

models.name: The Waterlog
models.description: Finished Board Specs: 10' x 23 3/4" x 2 7/8'/ Volume 81.92L 9'4" x 23 1/4" x 2 7/8"/ Volume 74.94L For 'Tailored Dims', We'll reach out with a form to tell us what you're thinking about. A classic log, the Waterlog is our traditional style longboard designed to catch all the waves you want and roam tip to tail while perfecting your footwork. It’s got the volume that bigger surfers want, beginners need, and small days demand. Point-and-go on this trimming machine, take a stroll to sweet spot at the nose, or crank a full pivot-turn from the tail. If smaller, gentler waves are your groove, the Waterlog is your magic carpet. The Waterlog features a full outline, providing the perfect platform for walking the full length of the board. A flatter nose rocker with a slight concave maximizes lift and stability when standing up front. After it’s noticeable “hips", the tail end of the Waterlog tapers to a squash tail. Increased tail rocker lift and a bellied bottom let the board roll and pivot with surprising ease and quickness from the tail. Rounded, 60/40 rails keep volume for side-to-side stability, and run back through the tail, helping control trimming speed to lock into the pocket of peelers.

models.name: The Steamer
models.description: Finished Board Specs 8'-0″ x 22-7/8″ x 3-1/16″ / Volume 65.34 L For 'Tailored Dims', we'll reach out with a form to tell us what you're thinking about. This mini-tanker was built with the small-statured longboarder in mind. This full-volume, catch-anything, design is not only excellent for beginners or those transitioning from logs to shorter boards, but also for more advanced riders dropping into hollower waves where full-size longboards just don’t fit. Gently curving hips help this board sweep through turns like a dream, while the wider, classic longboard nose begs for you to cross-step forward.

models.name: Lovelace- Thick Lizzy
models.description: Finished Board Specs 7'-11" x 22" x 2-7/8" / Volume 54.2 L We’re stoked to work with well-known Santa Barbara shaper Ryan Lovelace to offer one of Ryan’s favorites, the foiled-out mini-glider he calls the Thick Lizzy. This board came from Ryan’s desire for a midlength to be fun in flatter faced and lower quality surf but could also perform without restriction in tighter pockets and pumping point breaks. The Thick Lizzy features an almost identical 50/50 outline, glider style 70/30 down rails, and a double concave through the tail. It rides high on the water's surface and is fast to get on plane through flatter sections but provides lots of hold and bite on the rail to handle steeper surf. It’s foil and deck shape makes it really walkable for a midlength, so it can be cheater fived for miles! The Thick Lizzy rides like a smaller board due to the constant curve in the outline and decently progressive tail rocker while still falling into that “flat & fast” category. You can get this board in foam direct from Ryan, and now, in wood, from Grain Surfboards

models.name: The CI Biscuit
models.description: Finished Board Specs 5'6" x 20" x 2-3/4" 5'8" x 20-1/4" x 2-3/4" 6'2" x 21.5" x 3" Grain Surfboards is honored to have partnered with Channel Islands Surfboards and Legendary shaper Al Merrick to offer the board Rob Machado made famous: the Biscuit. Short and full-volume all the way to the rails with a subtle single-to-double concave, Al successfully designed this board to catch waves like boards a foot longer. Even though the wood Biscuit is a meticulous copy of Al’s shape, surfing one is a different experience than you get on the Channel Islands originals. Expect a noticeable difference in weight that makes the wood Biscuit a smooth-riding, honey-colored chop-killer.

models.name: The MLBB
models.description: 'GreenRail' Custom Board Price is $1,850 Specs: 8'3" x 22 1/8" x 3 1/4" Volume: 63L This non-channel version of Christian Beamish's Midlength for Black Belt is our latest collaboration board—a perfect fusion of paddle power and effortless glide, built for steep, deep conditions. The 8'3 MLBB GreenRail can be a daily driver that boosts confidence and pushes your limits in bigger waves. This shape is a perfect blend of speed-egg elements and Hawaiian-inspired design, offering a versatile and high-performance riding experience. Christian Beamish is a surfer, shaper and writer living in Ventura, California. Inspired by the high performance and big wave surfing of the late 1970s/early 80s in Australia and Hawai’i, Beamish shapes boards for “power-flow” surfing: that is, wave riding based on positioning and going with the wave, not against it. Beamish is known for channel bottom designs in single, twin, and “two-plus-one” fin configurations. A key difference between the channel bottom and the non-channel (besides the obvious one) is the fin setup. This non-channel version can have either a single or two-plus-one fin setup whereas the channeled MLBB can only be set up as a single.
